stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the key concepts, visual model and worked explanation.

blocks.title: Abstraction
blocks.text: Focus on the information needed to solve the problem and ignore irrelevant detail. For a journey-time estimate, distance and speed matter; car colour does not.

blocks.title: Decomposition
blocks.text: Break a complex problem into smaller, manageable parts that can be designed and checked separately, such as collecting inputs, calculating a result and displaying it.

blocks.title: Algorithmic thinking
blocks.text: Plan precise, logical steps in the correct order so that the problem can be solved. Decide what happens first, what must be checked and how the answer is produced.

blocks.title: IPO helps organise the steps
blocks.text: Input–Process–Output (IPO) is a useful way to plan the parts of a solution: gather the needed data, process it and show the result. IPO supports decomposition; it is not a replacement for algorithmic thinking.

blocks.title: Put ADA together
blocks.text: Journey-time calculator: abstract to distance and speed; decompose into input, checking, calculation and output; then order the steps to calculate and display hours.

blocks.title: Visual model · Computational Thinking — ADA
blocks.caption: Abstraction selects the needed details; decomposition separates tasks; algorithmic thinking orders them. IPO supports the plan.

blocks.title: Worked example · Plan a journey-time calculator using abstraction, decomposition, algorithmic thinking and IPO.
blocks.text: ABSTRACTION: retain distance and speed; ignore details such as car colour that do not affect this estimate. DECOMPOSITION: break the task into getting inputs, checking the speed, calculating time and displaying the answer. IPO: input distance = 60 km and speed = 30 km/h; process distance ÷ speed; output journey time in hours. ALGORITHMIC THINKING: in order, collect the values, check speed is greater than zero, divide 60 by 30, then display the result. OUTPUT: 2 hours, assuming constant speed. Each ordered step has a clear purpose and can be checked.

items: abstraction — Keeping the important details of a problem while ignoring irrelevant information.
decomposition — Breaking a complex problem into smaller, manageable parts.
algorithmic thinking — Planning a logical, ordered sequence of steps to solve a problem.
algorithm — A precise sequence of steps or instructions to solve a problem.
IPO — Input–Process–Output: a planning tool for what data goes in, what is done with it and what result comes out.

questions.prompt: Which ADA skill ignores irrelevant information?
questions.feedback: Abstraction focuses on what matters for a solution.

questions.prompt: Which ADA skill breaks a complex problem into manageable smaller tasks?

questions.prompt: What does algorithmic thinking focus on?
